chunks: Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Lakhmi narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Uthman ibn Salih, Mutalib ibn Shu'ayb al-Azdi, and Ahmad ibn Rashid (the Basrans) narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Hammad narrated to us from Abi Hazim al-Madini, who said: Imran ibn Umar ibn Sa'id al-Musaybi narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abi Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Indeed, for Allah are three sanctities: whoever preserves them, Allah will preserve for him his religious and worldly affairs; and whoever does not preserve them, Allah will not preserve anything for him: the sanctity of Islam, my sanctity, and the sanctity of my progeny (Ahl al-Bayt).

key_terms.حَرَمَاتٍ: Sanctities or things to be respected/protected

ai.seo_question: What are the three sanctities that ensure divine protection for one's religion and worldly affairs?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal underscores the triad of sanctities—Islam, the Prophet, and his progeny (Ahl al-Bayt)—as the foundational pillars for comprehensive divine protection in both spiritual and temporal realms. In Shia scholarship, the inclusion of 'my sanctity' and 'the sanctity of my progeny' highlights the inseparable link between prophetic authority and the Imams, serving as a criterion for preserving the integrity of the faith. Neglecting these specific sanctities is portrayed not merely as a ritual lapse but as a fundamental breach that compromises the believer's entire state of being.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-173 Suleiman ibn Ahmad al-Lakhmy narrated that Yahya ibn Uthman ibn Salih, Mutalib ibn Shoayb al-Azodi and Ahmad ibn Rashid - the two from Basra , on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Himad, on the authority of Abi Hazim al-Madinee, on the authority of Imran ibn Umar ibn Sa’id al-Mosayeb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Abi Sa’id al-Khidry that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,

“There are three things to respect so that God will protect your religion and worldly affairs. And if you disrespect them, God will not protect anything for you. These three things to respect are Islam, me and my Itrat (being God’s Book and my progeny).”
